subject: Vendor onboarding: PO assignment, spend cap confirmation & line-item cleanup

Subject: Vendor onboarding: initial PO request and spend cap guidance

Hi Liam / team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood. To get OrchardCloud set up as a vendor and to move toward a PO we need: 
- Completed vendor onboarding form (attached)
- Confirmation of annual spend cap you want encoded on the PO and in our billing guardrails
- Preferred invoice line-item mapping (subscription vs professional services) 

Can you return the filled form and a sample invoice or proposed line-items? If you have a preferred PO template we can also stamp a PO number and send the signed stub.

Attachments: OrchardCloud_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf)

Next steps I’ll take after those are in: loop in Finance to issue PO number, set the spend cap in billing controls, and create the initial invoice routing.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: initial PO request and spend cap guidance

Jonas —

Thanks for the checklist. I’ve attached the onboarding form and our standard invoice template (we usually present two lines: Platform subscription and Implementation support). For onboarding we typically ask that the supplier set a temporary spend cap while the first two invoices clear — normally $75,000 annual, but we can do $60,000 if Redwood policy prefers a lower default.

Attached: OrchardCloud_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (completed), Sample_Invoice_OrchardCloud.pdf

If you need us to recategorize the support line into subscription for the first quarter, we can supply a corrected invoice. Let us know desired PO number format and spend cap to include.

—Liam

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Vendor onboarding: initial PO request and spend cap guidance

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding OrchardCloud’s completed form and sample invoice. Please do the following: 
1) Issue a PO number and return a signed stub to OrchardCloud (I’ve asked for PO format: PO-YYYY-XXXXX).
2) Set the billing spend cap to $60,000 annual (OrchardCloud agreed to that if it’s our preference).
3) Update line-item mapping so "Implementation support" is billed under Subscription for Q1 only; we’ll revert after Q1 unless they supply a change request.
4) Confirm whether we should block invoices above the spend cap or simply alert Accounting for manual approval.

Attachments: LineItems_OrchardCloud_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Let me know if you need any legal countersigning before issuing PO.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: OrchardCloud Finance <finance@orchardcloud.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor onboarding: initial PO request and spend cap guidance

Jonas —

PO issued: PO-2026-68321. Attached is the signed PO stub. We set the active spend cap to $60,000 per 12 months and configured billing guards to flag any invoice attempts that would push month-to-date spend to >85% of that cap.

Line-item handling: we mapped "Implementation support" into the Subscription GL for the first quarter as requested. Moving forward: if OrchardCloud wants to change the mapping after Q1, they should send a formal change request to finance@redwood.com and we’ll process a line-item reclassification.

Options on over-cap handling:
- Block invoices automatically (requires a 48-hour SR from Legal to adjust vendor T&Cs)
- Allow but route to Accounting for manual approval (current default)

Which option do we want? I recommend manual approval for the first 60 days so we don’t block urgent billings while accounts reconcile.

Attachments: PO_stub_PO-2026-68321.pdf (application/pdf)

—Marissa Cole
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
